title: Valid Subarrays With Exactly One Peak
summary: Given an integer array nums of length n and an integer k, find the number of subarrays that contain exactly one peak within the range i-k to i+k, where a peak is defined as an element greater than its neighbors.
statement: Given an integer array nums of length n and an integer k, find the number of subarrays that contain exactly one peak within the range i-k to i+k, where a peak is defined as an element greater than its neighbors.
constraints: A global peak i satisfies 0<i<n-1 and nums[i] exceeds both neighbors.
A valid subarray contains exactly one such peak p, with each endpoint at distance at most k from p.
reference_solution:
def count_single_peak_subarrays(nums,k):
    peaks=[i for i in range(1,len(nums)-1) if nums[i]>nums[i-1] and nums[i]>nums[i+1]];answer=0
    for index,peak in enumerate(peaks):
        left=max(0,peak-k,peaks[index-1]+1 if index else 0)
        right=min(len(nums)-1,peak+k,peaks[index+1]-1 if index+1<len(peaks) else len(nums)-1)
        answer+=(peak-left+1)*(right-peak+1)
    return answer

For peak p, its left endpoint is bounded by p-k, the array start, and one past the previous peak; the right is symmetric.
Multiply the independent numbers of left and right endpoint choices.
Neighbor-peak bounds enforce uniqueness, distance bounds enforce k, and every valid subarray is counted once at its sole peak.
